reading.rtitle: Handover Note — Northwind Logistics · From Patrícia to Tom
paras: Northwind Logistics renewed for twelve months on June the twenty-eighth, and from August the account moves to Tom Becker. I am moving to a new portfolio of premium accounts, so this note is my handover. The most important thing to know is that Northwind is not a difficult customer, but it is a customer that remembers everything. After the outage in March, they almost left. What brought them back was continuity: the same person, the same day for the call, and numbers every month.

Here is what I recommend. Keep having the monthly call on the first Thursday of the month: David has asked twice not to move it. Remember to send the usage report before the fifth, because finance uses it in their own meeting on the sixth. Avoid promising new features on the call. Richard, the executive sponsor, has agreed to support the renewal on one condition: no surprises. If a feature is not on the roadmap, say that you need to check with product, and follow up in writing.

Two quirks. David prefers talking on the phone to reading long emails, so keep emails to five lines. And the finance team hates receiving the report as a PDF: they want the spreadsheet. Their biggest pain point is still the monthly report, and the plan is to finish automating it by October. I have agreed to join your first two calls with them, and I suggest shadowing me on the call in July before you take over. I will also give you a warm introduction to David and Richard, so that nobody receives a cold email from a new name.
reading.source: Adapted for class use from a customer success handover note

gist.prompt: What is the best one-line summary of this note?
choices: It explains why Northwind almost left in March and who was responsible.
It passes the account to Tom: what to keep doing, what to avoid, the quirks, and what Patrícia has agreed to do.
It is a proposal to change the monthly call and the report format.

This note says that Northwind is a customer that remembers everything. Which of your own accounts is like that, and what does it remember?
The note has two quirks. What is one quirk of a real customer of yours that is not written anywhere?
If you left one of your accounts tomorrow, what is the one sentence that your colleague must read first?

listenings.text: Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. I read your handover note for Tom, and it is very good. Just two things before Friday. First, remember why handovers are a risk. Most of the customers who leave in the first year after a renewal leave after a change of manager, not after an outage. So please avoid disappearing on the day of the handover. I want you on the first two calls, and I have already told Tom to expect that. Second, I suggest adding one sentence at the end of the note: what this customer is afraid of. For Northwind, I think it is surprises. If Tom knows that, he will make the right decisions without asking you. And congratulations again on the new portfolio. You earned it.

Patrícia, it is David. Thank you for calling me before the email went out. I will be honest, I was worried when I heard. The last time our account manager changed, nobody told us for a month, and we only found out when a new name appeared on an invoice. So this is already better. I have one request. Please promise to stay on the first calls, so that Tom does not start from zero with us. And tell Tom that I am happy to show him the warehouse. If he sees the workflow in real life, he will understand our reports much faster. Congratulations on the new accounts. We will miss you on Thursdays.
